raw_response:
I have farmed these 9 mu for 30 years. Never went to school, but I know this land. My son works in Shijiazhuang and sends money home, so we can buy inputs, but I still count every yuan. I watch Old Wang and Auntie Li — if their crops look good, I copy them.

For wheat: I sowed improved seed last autumn, same as Old Wang. At sowing I put one full bag of compound fertilizer per mu — those are 50 jin bags. Now spring is starting, I will topdress with 25 jin of urea per mu. Last year I put 20 jin, but Old Wang put 25 and his wheat was thicker and greener. I trust what I see with my own eyes. I irrigate four times: once in winter if it is dry, once when the wheat turns green, once when the stems grow tall, and once when the heads come out. My well has enough water. I spray twice — once for weeds, once if I see insects. Before sowing wheat I use the rotary machine to turn the soil. Last year I got about 900 jin per mu, this year I expect the same.

For maize: After we cut the wheat in June, I plant hybrid maize seed — the yellow kind from the seed dealer that everyone in the village uses. I put about 40 jin of compound fertilizer per mu at sowing, putting it right in the rows. When the plants are knee-high, I spread 20 jin of urea per mu. I irrigate three times: at sowing if the soil is dry, when the plants are tall, and when the ears are filling. I spray twice for weeds and corn borers. I don't plough for maize — I plant right after wheat harvest, no-tillage, so I don't miss the season. Last year I got about 1100 jin per mu, this year I hope for the same.

Fertilizer prices went up again. It hurts. But I would rather put a bit too much than too little. A bad harvest means disaster — we need the grain and the cash from selling the surplus. Wasting some fertilizer is just money spent. I will stick with what worked last year. If everyone around me changes, I might change a little, but probably not. I have seen too many people try new things and fail.
